Increasing concentrations of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are the primary cause of recent climate change. These heat-trapping gases come from a variety of human activities, including burning fossil fuels. When greenhouse gases are emitted into the atmosphere, many remain there for long time periods ranging from a decade to many millennia. EPA’s greenhouse gas-related indicators present trends in greenhouse gas emissions, the resulting atmospheric concentrations, and the corresponding warming effect they have on the planet.

This feature builds on EPA’s Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator by presenting future projections for the three most prominent long-lived greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide. Carbon dioxide is measured in parts per million (ppm); the others in parts per billion (ppb).
